
{{alias}}( order, norm, uplo, N, K, AB, LDAB, work )
    Computes the value of the one norm, Frobenius norm, infinity norm, or the
    element of largest absolute value of a real symmetric band matrix `A`.

    Indexing is relative to the first index. To introduce an offset, use typed
    array views.

    Parameters
    ----------
    order: string
        Row-major (C-style) or column-major (Fortran-style) order. Must be
        either 'row-major' or 'column-major'.

    norm: string
        Specifies the value to be returned. Must be one of the following: 'max'
        (the largest absolute value of any element), 'one' (the one norm, i.e.,
        the maximum column sum), 'inf' (the infinity norm, i.e., the maximum row
        sum), or 'fro' (the Frobenius norm).

    uplo: string
        Specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part of the band matrix
        `A` is supplied. Must be either 'upper' or 'lower'.

    N: integer
        Order of the matrix `A`.

    K: integer
        Number of super-diagonals of the matrix `A` if `uplo` is 'upper', or the
        number of sub-diagonals if `uplo` is 'lower'.

    AB: Float64Array
        Input band matrix `A` stored in banded format.

    LDAB: integer
        Stride of the first dimension of `AB` (a.k.a., leading dimension of the
        matrix `AB`).

    work: Float64Array
        Workspace array. Only referenced when computing the one or infinity
        norm, in which case the array must have at least `N` elements.

    Returns
    -------
    out: number
        Norm value.

    Examples
    --------
    > var AB = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 0.0, 2.0, 1.0, 3.0 ] );
    > var work = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 2 );
    > {{alias}}( 'column-major', 'max', 'upper', 2, 1, AB, 2, work )
    3.0


{{alias}}.ndarray( norm, uplo, N, K, AB, sa1, sa2, oa, work, sw, ow )
    Computes the value of the one norm, Frobenius norm, infinity norm, or the
    element of largest absolute value of a real symmetric band matrix `A` using
    alternative indexing semantics.

    While typed array views mandate a view offset based on the underlying
    buffer, the offset parameters support indexing semantics based on starting
    indices.

    Parameters
    ----------
    norm: string
        Specifies the value to be returned. Must be one of the following: 'max'
        (the largest absolute value of any element), 'one' (the one norm, i.e.,
        the maximum column sum), 'inf' (the infinity norm, i.e., the maximum row
        sum), or 'fro' (the Frobenius norm).

    uplo: string
        Specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part of the band matrix
        `A` is supplied. Must be either 'upper' or 'lower'.

    N: integer
        Order of the matrix `A`.

    K: integer
        Number of super-diagonals of the matrix `A` if `uplo` is 'upper', or the
        number of sub-diagonals if `uplo` is 'lower'.

    AB: Float64Array
        Input band matrix `A` stored in banded format.

    sa1: integer
        Stride of the first dimension of `AB`.

    sa2: integer
        Stride of the second dimension of `AB`.

    oa: integer
        Starting index for `AB`.

    work: Float64Array
        Workspace array. Only referenced when computing the one or infinity
        norm.

    sw: integer
        Stride length for `work`.

    ow: integer
        Starting index for `work`.

    Returns
    -------
    out: number
        Norm value.

    Examples
    --------
    > var AB = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 0.0, 2.0, 1.0, 3.0 ] );
    > var work = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 2 );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( 'max', 'upper', 2, 1, AB, 1, 2, 0, work, 1, 0 )
    3.0

    See Also
    --------
